headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading errors if next-ai-draw-io outputs are fed into pipecat’s shared-bus, multi-service pipelines.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: next-ai-draw-io ingests PDFs, text, images, and draw.io content and uses MCP plus natural-language tool use; pipecat supports shared-bus session state and many downstream services. A direct injection path is plausible if A’s generated content is passed into B’s prompts or tools, but the pairwise bridge is not documented, so I avoid high.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are copied into agent_b prompts or shared bus messages, injection risk materializes.
IF agent_b treats upstream text as instructions without provenance checks, attacker-controlled content can steer tool use.
mitigations: Disable automatic handoff from A to B; require manual review of A outputs.
Add a provenance tag to every A output before B consumes it.
Strip instructions from imported text and diagrams before passing to B.
Run B with a prompt firewall or instruction delimiter policy.
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware parsing between the agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A handles API keys and broad network egress; B touches conversation state, audio/video/text, and can call many third-party STT/LLM/TTS services. If they share a workspace or bus, sensitive document content from A can flow into B and then out to external APIs. The exact shared channel is not documented, so this is inferred rather than directly evidenced.
conditions: IF A and B share files, stdin/stdout, or a bus carrying document text, leakage becomes plausible.
IF B is configured to send conversation state to a third-party STT/LLM/TTS provider, upstream content can leave the boundary.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces and OS users.
Remove secrets from A inputs before any transfer to B.
Disable B services that forward text/audio to external APIs.
Audit logs for document text and redact sensitive fields.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policy.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A can use MCP and broad network egress; B has shared-bus session scope and multiple-instance shared state. That creates overlapping mutable surfaces if both are wired to the same resources, even though neither profile proves unrestricted same-directory filesystem writes. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same shared bus or mutable backend, state races can occur.
IF A’s MCP tools and B’s services target the same resource, last-writer-wins conflicts are possible.
mitigations: Assign separate resource namespaces to A and B.
Turn on locking or single-writer mode for shared resources.
Avoid concurrent writes during the same session.
Log and diff all mutations from each agent.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control to shared backends.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces AI-assisted visualizations from documents, and B is a real-time voice/chat framework with many downstream services. If B consumes A’s generated facts or diagrams as authoritative input, errors can cascade into spoken responses, API calls, or other actions. Because B’s pipeline is action-capable by default, the blast radius is larger than medium.
conditions: IF B renders or acts on A’s extracted facts without verification, hallucinations can propagate.
IF A’s diagram/text output is used as source-of-truth for B’s downstream actions, errors become operational.
mitigations: Require human review of A outputs before B uses them.
Add a verification step in B for any A-derived facts.
Limit B to read-only summarization when consuming A outputs.
Disable automatic action-taking on untrusted inputs.
requires-engineering: implement source attribution and confidence gating.

E_compliance.rationale: A explicitly handles API keys and document files, while B can route text/audio/video through many third-party providers and analytics services. If regulated or sensitive documents from A are fed into B, retention and residency obligations may diverge across providers. The profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF A processes regulated documents and B forwards derived text/audio to external providers, compliance obligations may diverge.
IF B’s provider settings retain transcripts or analytics beyond A’s policy, retention mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Classify data before routing from A to B.
Disable analytics and transcript retention in B.
Use only providers with matching residency and retention terms.
Keep regulated documents out of B’s pipeline.
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing and retention controls.
